# James Larson: weather forecasts

> Personal forecasting pages. The WxChallenge page compares numerical weather models for the
> current WxChallenge city (a North American college forecasting contest: forecast the next
> day's high, low, max sustained wind and precipitation, scored 06Z to 06Z), builds a
> bias-corrected consensus, and verifies every model against observations. The pages draw
> their tables with JavaScript; the files below hold the same data as plain text and JSON.

## WxChallenge

- [Forecast brief](https://jameslarsonclimate.github.io/website/weather-forecasts/data/wxchallenge/brief.md): start here. A short Markdown summary: target day and deadline, every model's forecast, the consensus and its weights, ensemble percentiles, precipitation chances, each model's hourly temperature, wind, accumulated precipitation and cloud cover through the day, observed clouds (GOES satellite and METAR) for past days and hour by hour today, each model's bias, MAE and error points this period, every verified day's observations, errors and points (the full verification table), each day's precipitation chances against what fell, how today is going so far, the scoring rules, and a step-by-step method for making a forecast from it.
- [forecast.json](https://jameslarsonclimate.github.io/website/weather-forecasts/data/wxchallenge/forecast.json): full forecast for the target day, including every ensemble member and the consensus method.
- [verification.json](https://jameslarsonclimate.github.io/website/weather-forecasts/data/wxchallenge/verification.json): every verified day this period with each model's forecast, error and points, the observations, and precipitation-chance calibration.
- [today.json](https://jameslarsonclimate.github.io/website/weather-forecasts/data/wxchallenge/today.json): the day in progress, models against the observations so far.
- [NWS Area Forecast Discussion (TBW)](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=TBW&issuedby=TBW&product=AFD&format=txt&version=1&glossary=0): the latest forecaster discussion from the NWS office for the current city (Tampa). When the city changes, the brief's "Raw data" section has the right office.

## Asked for a WxChallenge forecast?

Read the brief, check its "Generated" time against the current time, then follow its
"How to use this brief" section. Give whole °F for the high and low, whole kt for wind and
precipitation to 0.01", and explain any departure from the consensus using the
verification data.
